newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end Tokyo down, but off low.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end Tokyo down, but off low.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Tokyo trade a bit easier on Tuesday, as lingering speculation over the outlook for Japanese interest rates poured cold water on the recent rally, traders said.

Prices fell from the onset of trade as a news agency report on Monday, quoting a senior official in one of Japan's ruling parties as saying a rise in the discount rate will probably be considered after elections, invited sales, they said.

Shizuka Kamei, the Liberal Democratic Party's publicity chief, was quoted on Monday as saying that a rise in Japan's official discount rate, and other interest rates, will probably be considered after the October 20 general election.
"The morning sales were caused by Kamei's comments," said a city bank trader.
The selling took the contract down to its day's low of 99.30, but traders refrained from further sales as many believe the comments were mere lip service to voters, they said.
They said the comments have not altered views that the Bank of Japan will keep rates steady at least until next spring.
"Traders are reacting calmly to such comments, as they are coming out before the election," said one brokerage trader.
Prices rose briefly in the afternoon, to the day's high of 99.35, on weak economic data, dealers said.

Japan's private-sector machinery orders for August, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, fell a seasonally adjusted 11.1 percent from the previous month, the Economic Planning Agency said.
"But the buying soon ebbed as there's an overall feeling that prices have risen enough recently," said the city bank dealer.
Turnover for the March futures was 39,394 contracts.
The BOJ maintained its neutral money market stance this morning, injecting 500 billion yen into the money market and nearly offsetting a projected fund shortage of 510 billion yen.
Japan's key overnight call rate stood at 0.45 percent as of 0800 GMT, unchanged from the previous day.
About 345 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.52 percent, unchanged from October 4, when they were last issued. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-5473-3710)
